api.description: Create a sandbox

fields.description: Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key returns what this key already did instead of doing it again. Leave it out and the plugin sends a new random key.

Accepts the Mac lease of a macOS sandbox (the template's `minimumLease`, `GET /v1/templates`): a whole Mac for the org for at least 24 hours, billed whatever the sandbox does. Required to create one: without it the create is `400 minimum_lease_required` and nothing is placed.
Sets `archiveAt` to now plus this many seconds: the sandbox is stopped then if it is running. 0 or absent: none.

Absent: 1800 (30 minutes). The plan decides, and a value is honoured or refused, never silently replaced: a paid sandbox takes 300-1800 (5 to 30 minutes) in whole minutes, as sent, and 0 (off) where the plan allows always on (else `403 spec_not_allowed`); below 300 (1-299), above 1800, negative or not a multiple of 60 is `400 bad_request`. The free sandbox is fixed at 1800: any other value is `403 spec_not_allowed`, a plan limit (older servers: `403 permission_denied`). A refused create makes no sandbox. The reply's `autoSuspendAfterSeconds` shows the effective value. Separately, an account an admin gave manual lifecycle (`GET /v1/me` `manualLifecycle`) sends 120-86400 idle seconds, or 0 never (docs/idle-suspend.md).

Sets `deleteAt` to now plus this many seconds (60-86400, else 400): the sandbox is then deleted, whatever its state, so it cannot outlive a client that died (`instabox run` sets it). 0 or absent: never. A server without this field ignores it.
Default: running.

fields.type: { env?: string, file?: string, secret: string }[]
fields.description: Direct (delivery env) Secrets from this org, each as a variable and/or a home file. Real values enter the sandbox; prefer proxy Secrets for HTTPS API keys. A fork that sends none of secrets, envSecrets and directSecrets copies its source's selection.

Environment variables for the whole sandbox: every login shell exports them (exec, SSH, the terminal and what they start), from the first command on and again after each start and resume. Names match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}$`; `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `HOME`, `HOSTNAME`, `IFS`, `LOGNAME`, `OLDPWD`, `PATH`, `PWD`, `SHELL`, `SHLVL`, `USER`, bash's readonly `BASHOPTS`, `BASH_VERSINFO`, `EUID`, `PPID`, `SHELLOPTS` and `UID`, the session's `TERM`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, the trust roots `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, and names starting `INSTABOX_` or `SSH_` are reserved (set them per exec); values have no NUL bytes; names and values at most 32 KiB together. Not on Windows templates (400). On macOS, bash and zsh login shells export them, and zsh's special parameters (`status`, `path`, `options`, `HISTSIZE`, `USERNAME`, ...) and `ZDOTDIR` are reserved too. Fixed at create: a fork takes its source's, a create from a snapshot only its own. An exec's `envs`, a Vault item and an env Secret of the same name win. Not Secrets: anything in the sandbox can read the values, and the sandbox shows only the names (`envNames`). The values are stored encrypted at rest; a site without the Secret master key refuses env (400 bad_request).

Explicit env Secret names from this org; omitted or [] selects none. No all mode; null is rejected. Real values enter the sandbox. Shorthand for directSecrets entries with env = the Secret's name; not sent together with directSecrets.

When no host has room for the sandbox right now, refuse the create at once with `503 no_capacity` (`retryable`; nothing is created, there is no operation and the `Idempotency-Key` is not kept) instead of answering 202 with an operation that then fails with `no_capacity`. Every other check and the rest of the create are unchanged; a host that had room can still fill up before the operation places the sandbox. The check does not ask for a host with the secret proxy, which a create with `secrets` or `envSecrets` needs: if only hosts without it have room, the create is accepted and its operation fails with `no_capacity`. A create from a snapshot that no host can start now is refused too, instead of being created stopped. A server without this field ignores it, or, if it already refuses unknown body keys, answers `400 unknown_field`.

GPUs for the sandbox: `TYPE` (one GPU) or `TYPE:COUNT`, such as `l4` or `l4:2`, a type of the GPU template's `gpuTypes` (`GET /v1/templates`). GPU sandboxes are for paid plans: a free org's create is `403 template_not_allowed`. The count is one of the type's `counts`: the powers of two up to its `maxPerMachine`, such as 1, 2 or 4 (a count of 3 would leave a 4-GPU host one GPU that no pair fits). An org's running sandboxes hold at most 20 GPUs in all (`403 template_limit` past it, also on a start, resume or wake; a stopped or paused sandbox holds none). The template defaults to `gpu`, and the size comes from the type: one of its `sizes`, per GPU (`l4:2` gets twice the vCPUs and memory, the same disk; `vcpus` and `memMiB` pick another of its sizes, multiplied). An unknown type, a template without GPU support or a count not in `counts` (`l4:3`) is `400 bad_request` naming the counts. With `snapshotId` of a GPU sandbox's snapshot, the snapshot's GPU type with any of its `counts` (`l4:4` from a one-GPU snapshot), sized from that count; another type is `400 bad_request`, and absent `gpu` gets the snapshot's own count (a snapshot of a 3-GPU sandbox, from before the rule, is `400 bad_request` until `gpu` names one of the counts). GPUs are billed per GPU-hour while the sandbox runs, on top of its vCPUs and memory. Absent: no GPU (from a snapshot: the snapshot's GPU).

The sandbox's Linux user (`Machine.guestUser`), so `ssh <sandbox>` over your own network (Tailscale) logs in as the same name as on your computer. Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters; reserved names (`root`, `instabox`, the Debian base system's users and groups such as `sudo`, `systemd-*`) are refused with `400 invalid_guest_user`. Clients send the local username normalized (`DOMAIN\alice` and `alice@corp.example` become `alice`, lowercase, spaces become `_`) and nothing when that is not a valid name. Absent: `user`; with `snapshotId`, the snapshot's user. Ignored (the sandbox gets `dev`) for templates without the `guest-user` capability. Fixed at create.
Deprecated: `snapshotId` under its old name (both: they must be equal). The reply carries a `Deprecation` header.

Maximum continuous runtime in minutes. -1 is unlimited; 0 sleeps immediately. Independent of idle auto-pause; whichever condition is reached first pauses the sandbox. On a free machine the service sets it and only an admin session can change it: each run starts at 120 minutes and grows with use up to 480 (commands, file access, port requests, terminal or SSH traffic and CPU load count as use; activity leases and wake calls do not): https://instabox.sh/docs/machines/auto-pause#runtime-on-the-free-plan. A free machine that is not running reports 480, the most a run can last. The response reports the current limit from runStartedAt; it can change during the run. Paid machines default to -1 and their users can change this setting. Max-run suspension starts a cooldown, returning 409 machine_cooldown with Retry-After on every wake path, except on Pro and higher plans, which have none. By default it is 5 to 20 minutes (5 plus a random 0 to 15) for the first such pause in a row on the free plan. Back-to-back pauses on the free plan rest longer (60 to 75, then 120 to 135 minutes): "Longer cooldowns on the free plan" at https://instabox.sh/docs/machines/auto-pause#longer-cooldowns-on-the-free-plan. Once cooldown ends, 0 still refuses wake with 409 max_run_disabled until changed.
Like vcpus: the memory (MiB) of one of your sizes, such as 8192 with vcpus 4; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`.
String labels. At most 32 keys of 1-64 characters `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, values of at most 512 characters, 8 KiB as JSON.

The Mac model of a macOS template with `models`, by its `name`: the sandbox runs on that model's Macs, at one of that model's sizes. Absent: the template's `pool`, or its first open model when that pool's model is `closed`. With `snapshotId`: the model to run the snapshot on, at that model's sizes; absent, the snapshot's own `model` unless it is closed.

1-63 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, starting with a letter or digit; unique among the org's sandboxes. Absent or empty: `box-` and 8 random hex digits (the operation's `machineId` and the sandbox carry it).

fields.type: { allowCidrs?: string[], allowDomains?: string[], outbound: restricted | open }
fields.description: A sandbox's outbound network policy: where it may connect to on the internet. It only narrows: a destination the platform blocks stays blocked. Inbound access (SSH, exec, published ports) is not affected. A fork starts with its source's policy. Domains are allowed through DNS: the sandbox's resolver answers only the listed names and opens the firewall for the addresses it returns, for as long as the DNS record lives, so a program must use the system resolver, and a connection to an address that no allowed name resolved to is refused unless a range lists it. It is not strict data-loss prevention: a site that shares an address with an allowed one (a CDN) is reachable too.

The org the sandbox counts against and is shared with (`GET /v1/orgs`); you must be a member. Absent: your personal org, or with `snapshotId` the snapshot's org (a sandbox from a snapshot lives in the snapshot's org; another is `400 bad_request`). Secret selections always resolve within this org. The org's sandbox limit and, on the free tier, its monthly included usage apply (`429 quota_exceeded`, `402 credit_exhausted`).

Storage (`/data`) size in GiB. The disks come with the size: storage gets the size's (20 GiB on api.instabox.sh), or a snapshot's storage size when that is larger. Absent or exactly that size: accepted; any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` whose message names the size's storage next to what was asked; 0 or a negative is `400 bad_request`. To get more storage, grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`: a running sandbox's storage grows live, and a shrink applies while it is stopped, at its next boot. The SDKs' `diskGiB` (TypeScript) and `persistent_disk_gib` (Python) are this field; `diskGiB` in a REST body is `400 unknown_field`.

Admins only: the host pool to place the sandbox in and no other (docs/hybrid-pools.md), "default" included. With snapshotId it must be the snapshot's pool. Absent: the user's pool assignment, else the server's placement.createPools.
Wait in the GPU queue, or for a macOS sandbox in the Mac queue (`CreateMachineRequest.queue`, `StartMachineRequest.queue`); `{}` waits up to an hour for a GPU, up to 7 days for a Mac.

System files size in GiB. Like persistentDiskGiB: system files get the template's size (or the snapshot's); naming any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` (the message names the size's root disk), 0 or a negative `400 bad_request`; grow it later with `PATCH /v1/machines/{id}`.

Proxy selection only. All includes current and future proxy Secrets in the sandbox's org. Explicit names resolve to stable IDs. An empty array selects none. Deleting and recreating a name does not restore an explicit grant. Null is rejected.
Create from this snapshot of yours: its system files and storage (empty storage for a system-files-only snapshot).

The template to create from (`GET /v1/templates`, one with `creatable` true), optionally with a version as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`, the same as `templateVersion`). Absent (and no `snapshotId` or `templateVersion`): agent-browser. An unknown or retired one is refused with `400 bad_request` whose message lists the templates your plan can create from. The free plan creates from agent-browser, android, omarchy or ci only; another template is refused with `403 template_not_allowed`. A create from a snapshot is not limited.

Default: the version `GET /v1/templates` marks `latest`. `templateId` may name it instead, as `id@version` (e.g. `agent-browser@2026-10-15.4`); both at once must agree. A version the template does not have is `400 bad_request` whose message lists its versions, newest first, the `latest` (or `default`) one tagged.
False disables legacy Vault delivery. Org Secret selections are independent.

Absent: the default size (4 vCPUs, 8 GiB memory; `limits.machineSpec`). From a snapshot with `sizeLocked` (not of a GPU sandbox): the vCPUs and memory of the sandbox it was saved from (the snapshot's `defaultSpec`), absent or named; any other is `400 spec_not_allowed` stating the snapshot's size, and that size is `403 spec_not_allowed` while the org's plan does not offer it (upgrade the plan). A snapshot without `sizeLocked` (saved before this rule) takes any size below. Else one of the org's sizes (`GET /v1/orgs` `allowedSpecs`: the default, its plan's others and any size an admin granted the org; on api.instabox.sh free 4/8192 only, Pro 2/4096, 4/8192, 8/16384, Builder 2/4096 up to 16/32768, Team and Enterprise 2/4096 up to 32/65536), or, from a template with a `pool` (macOS, Windows), its `defaultSpec` or one of its `sizes`, whatever the plan; name memMiB too when two of them have this many vCPUs. Anything else is refused with `400 spec_not_allowed`; 0 or a negative (no size) with `400 bad_request`.
